name: CA-46
label: Safe D

key_factors: Correa is an incumbent in a D+10 district with a large cash advantage
Pan has raised only ~$81k with minimal cash on hand
Polymarket prices Correa at ~96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Correa: a D+10 seat, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than 15-to-1 over Pan, whose campaign lacks the resources to compete. Markets price the race near certain for the Democrat, and no evidence suggests a serious challenge.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Correa or an unexpectedly strong Republican top-line showing in California could signal a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lou Correa seeks another term in a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, roughly $2.5 million on hand, while Republican David Pan has raised under $100,000 and has little cash remaining. No outside groups are spending meaningfully against the incumbent.

With no public polling of the race and no expert ratings, the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Correa heavily. Prediction markets give him roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. The forecast places the expected margin in the low twenties for Correa, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating, though uncertainty is somewhat elevated given the absence of direct polling.
